hypotheses.claim: For user-specific GUI/layout familiarity and open-set routing, a descriptor built from Qwen3.5's public LLM-facing projected visual token grid can match a private pre-merger vision tap closely enough that no Qwen-internal feature hook is justified.
hypotheses.why_it_matters: If supported, Frank can reuse the exact visual representation already required for semantic decode while keeping the runtime on stable public libmtmd surfaces.
hypotheses.strongest_counterhypothesis: Qwen3.5's merger/projection discards or distorts instance/layout geometry needed for calibrated familiarity, so pre-merger or independent retrieval features materially dominate.
hypotheses.falsifier: Projected-grid MVC is Pareto-dominated on false-familiarity/open-set calibration and task outcome by pre-merger or lightweight-independent features under matched screenshots and resource accounting.
hypotheses.cheapest_test: Frozen user-specific replay set; compare identical prototype and linear heads on projected-grid descriptors, HF-reference pre-merger descriptors, MobileCLIP2-S0 and DINOv3-S/16 descriptors.
hypotheses.expected_if_supported: Projected-grid reaches frozen tolerance on AUROC/FPR95/ECE/false-familiarity while minimizing duplicate encode cost and state movement.
hypotheses.expected_if_counter: Projected-grid shows systematic near-neighbor/UI-layout aliasing or calibration loss that disappears with pre-merger/independent features.

hypotheses.claim: Using libmtmd decoder-position metadata to preserve normalized x/y token topology in a coarse spatial-pyramid descriptor materially improves recurring GUI-state discrimination over global mean pooling without requiring pre-merger access.
hypotheses.strongest_counterhypothesis: Projected visual tokens are already sufficiently semantic/global that spatial binning adds dimensionality and sensitivity to window movement without useful discrimination gain.
hypotheses.falsifier: No held-out open-set/layout gain after translation/resize controls, or worse calibration/resource cost than global pooling.
hypotheses.cheapest_test: Compare global mean, global mean+variance, 2x2 pyramid, 3x3 pyramid and learned tiny projection under matched feature buffers and normalized decoder positions.

hypotheses.claim: Separating visual state into four lifetimes prevents state amplification and stale-feature errors while retaining same-cycle zero-reencode escalation: L0 frame/delta identity; L1 persistent compact MVC descriptor/prototypes; L2 ephemeral raw mtmd embedding buffer; L3 optional version-bound llama.cpp media/slot runtime cache.
hypotheses.strongest_counterhypothesis: The extra lifetime/type machinery adds complexity without measurable reliability or memory benefit compared with one versioned embedding cache.
hypotheses.falsifier: Unified embedding cache matches or beats the split design on restart correctness, stale-hit rate, memory/disk amplification, latency and implementation complexity under the same fixtures.
hypotheses.cheapest_test: Synthetic identity/restart matrix first; then Qwen3.5 target-runtime benchmark when target model/mmproj are available.

hypotheses.claim: Because Qwen3.5 mixes recurrent gated-delta layers with full attention, visual-prefix reuse/restart must bind LLM recurrent-state identity separately from raw visual embedding identity; visual embedding equality alone is insufficient to prove continuation-state equivalence.
hypotheses.strongest_counterhypothesis: Existing llama.cpp context/slot state machinery already guarantees sufficient equivalence and Frank-specific state typing adds no value beyond exact model/media identity.
hypotheses.falsifier: Across restart/save/restore tests, upstream state restoration is bit/behavior equivalent under all supported Frank media workflows and no additional Frank-visible state identity catches a failure.
hypotheses.cheapest_test: Same image/prompt with uninterrupted vs save/restore continuation, then changed image, mmproj swap, quant/model swap and token-budget change controls.

hypotheses.claim: MobileCLIP2-S0 is small enough to be a serious Frank-v0.1 counterbaseline rather than a strawman second encoder; it may beat reused Qwen projected features on familiarity/open-set while remaining operationally negligible.
hypotheses.strongest_counterhypothesis: Any duplicate image encode, even a small one, loses Pareto value once Qwen vision is already needed for changed/uncertain frames and projected-grid descriptors are sufficiently accurate.
hypotheses.falsifier: MobileCLIP2-S0 does not materially improve false-familiarity/calibration or safe decoder-bypass rate after total duplicate encode RAM/latency/power is counted.
hypotheses.cheapest_test: Run identical MVC-0 prototypes and MVC-1 linear head on MobileCLIP2-S0 vs reused Qwen projected descriptors; no text encoder in hot path unless needed for a separate task.
